description:

description:
Elevation, left version and right version side by side, not to scale: Each is a vertical stack of two pedestrian signal enclosures. The upper one is a regular pedestrian signal head showing a hand symbol and a walking person symbol. The lower one is the LED sign with the words USE TUNNEL in two lines and an arrow, a left-pointing arrow before USE on the left version and a right-pointing arrow after USE on the right version. The bracket label above says REGULAR PEDESTRIAN SIGNAL HEADS and the bracket below says LED SIGNS.

Dimensions: each enclosure is 18-1/2" wide and 18-3/4" high (both the regular head and the LED sign). The gap between the two enclosures is labeled SEE NOTE 4.

Title block: title "USE TUNNEL" Electric Sign, City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation, S. E. Rowe, General Manager, approved 3-18-92, Drawing No. S-58.14. Drawn LAR 03-05-92, checked KHC 03-11-92, supervised ERA 03-11-92, reviewed JEF 03-18-92. Printed page number 111. A footnote on the sheet reads * MEETING LADOT SPECIFICATIONS, tied to the asterisk in note 3.
notes:
1. The "USE TUNNEL" sign shall be internally illuminated by super LED diodes. The diodes shall emit red colored light. The sign background shall be black.
2. The sign message "USE TUNNEL" shall be 4" in height with brush stroke width of 1/2". The arrow shall be 6-1/2" long with brush stroke width of 1".
3. The sign housing shall consist of two (2) standard* pedestrian signal enclosures connected to one another in a vertical manner.
4. Minimum space shall be provided to allow free movement of door openings.
5. The "USE TUNNEL" electric sign shall be displayed only with the hand symbol of the pedestrian signal head.
* Meeting LADOT specifications.
title: Use Tunnel Electric Sign

The sign uses red super LED diodes on a black background and is housed in a standard pedestrian signal enclosure stacked vertically under the head. Both left arrow and right arrow versions are shown.

description:
Sign face: A rectangle 24" wide by 30" high with a dotted curved left arrow above the word ONLY. The solid dotted arrow points left, and a dashed outline of the mirror image right arrow is drawn over it to show the alternate message. Vertical dimensions from top: 3" from the top edge to the top of the arrow, 15-1/2" arrow height, 3" gap, 6" letter height for ONLY, 2-1/2" to the bottom edge, 30" overall. The arrow group is 13-1/2" wide. Lower left shows the notes.

Visor enclosure: An isometric view of a three-sided hood with a top panel and two side panels that taper from 17" deep at the top to 11" deep at the bottom. Overall 24" wide and 30" tall. The lower front corner of each side panel has a 2" Rad. rounded corner.

Title block: R3-5 Electric Sign, sheet 1 of 1, City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation, Drawing No. S-58.17. Drawn MT 7-08-08, checked RAR 7-09-08, T. E. JV 7-09-08, Sr. T. E. JW 7-09-08, Pr. T. E. SS 7-09-08. Approved July 9, 2008, signed for Rita L. Robinson, General Manager. Printed page number 112.
notes:
1. Sign shall be capable of displaying the following messages: A: Lunar white, R3-5L (left arrow with ONLY). Width of arrow is 1.5" stroke. B: Lunar white, R3-5R (right arrow with ONLY). Letters are series "C", 1" stroke.
2. Messages shall be formed with rows of fiber optic bundles spaced 0.50 inch (center to center).

9. For housing description, see LADOT Std. Dwg. No. S-58.21.

title: Sign Enclosure
summary: Housing, visor and parts list for the LADOT standard electric sign enclosure, drawing S-58.21, approved June 26, 2008. The housing is 26-3/4 inches wide and 26-3/4 or 32-3/4 inches tall, 8 inches deep, with a 17 inch to 11 inch visor. A 26 item parts table gives materials and quantities, and Detail A gives the 4-1/2 inch reinforcement plate.

description:
Train sign face: The housing is 26.75" wide by 32.75" high with a 24" by 30" face. The train symbol is 12" wide. Stainless steel link locks are called out on the right side. Vertical layout letters A to F run top to bottom: A is the top margin, B the train symbol body, C the track, D the gap, E the letter height of TRAIN and F the bottom margin. Horizontal spacing G and H are shown at the letters T, R, A, I, N.

Table of dimensions for the train sign: A = 1.5". B = 13". *C = 5". D = 3". E = 6". F = 1.5". G = 2.094". H = 2.688". Footnote: * Five 1" spaces to delineate the rail road track.

Bus sign face: The housing is 26.75" wide by 32.75" high with a 24" by 30" face, and 2.875" side margins on each side of the 24" face. The dotted bus symbol is 18.25" wide. Vertical dimensions: 2" top margin, 17.5" bus height, 2.5" gap, 6" letter height for BUS and 2" bottom margin, 30" overall.

Pedestrian head sign, train (not to scale): A rounded rectangle 16.25" wide by 14.5" high with the train symbol 8.3" wide and 12.5" tall, with 1" top and 1" bottom margins.

Pedestrian head sign, bus: A rounded rectangle 16.25" wide by 14.5" high with the dotted bus symbol 13" wide, 1.625" side margins and 12.5" tall, with 1" top and 1" bottom margins.

Visor enclosure: Isometric visor hood with dimensions drawn as 24', 17', 30' and 11', the same 24" wide, 30" tall hood that tapers from 17" to 11" deep seen on the R3-5 sign. The lower corners have a 2" Rad. callout.

Title block: Electric Train & Bus Warning Sign, City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation, Drawing No. S-58.23. Drawn MT 4-16-08, Pr. T. E. SS 6-26-08, approved June 26, 2008, Rita L. Robinson, General Manager. Printed page number 116.
notes:
1. Messages shall be formed by rows of fiber optic glass bundles.
2. Dual rows of fiber optic bundles shall be used to form the word "TRAIN". Letters in the bus warning sign message shall have a brush stroke of 1-inch. Bus symbol and letters shall also conform to the latest edition of the FHWA Standard Highway Signs book.
3. The front view of the train or bus shall be solid formed by rows of fiber optic glass bundles.
4. The color of the messages shall be yellow. The sign background shall be black.
5. Fiber optic glass bundles shall alternate between two or more lamp sources. In the event of a lamp failure, the sign shall continue to display a readable and discernable message.
6. Sign housing shall be equipped with four (4) 3/16" drain holes at the bottom.
7. The visor enclosure shall be fastened securely to the front frame of the sign.
8. Housing shall contain 4 1/2" x 4 1/2" x 1/4" reinforcement plate located on the top and bottom for use with the Pelco Astro Sign-Brac installation.
9. Refer to Std. Dwg. No. S-63.1.4 for the mounting assembly (T=46", L=29").
10. Sign shall conform to LADOT Specification No. 82-049-03.
11. For housing description see LADOT Std. Dwg. No. S-58.21.
Table footnote: * Five 1" spaces to delineate the rail road track.
title: Electric Train and Bus Warning Sign
summary: Fiber optic electric warning signs showing a train with the word TRAIN or a bus with the word BUS, drawing S-58.23, approved June 26, 2008. The signs are yellow on black and come in a 24 inch by 30 inch face and a 16.25 inch by 14.5 inch pedestrian head size. A table gives the letter and symbol spacing, and 11 notes cover fiber optic bundles, the FHWA sign book, drain holes and mounting.

description:
Section detail, controller cabinet front view (not to scale): A front elevation of the rack from top to bottom. The Model 2070 unit (2070 controller) has the City of Los Angeles label, an LCD, hex keypad, a function keypad with ESC, arrows, NEXT, YES, NO and ENT keys, an ACTIVE light, an AUX ON/OFF switch, a CONTRAST knob and a C50S serial port. Below are Input File I and Input File J, each a card file with slots. A 283LA sensor module is installed in slot 10 of each input file, shown with its channel lights and J1 serial port. Arrows point from the label 283LA sensor (see note 2) to each of the two modules. A DB9 serial cable (see note 3) runs from the 2070 port down the right side to the J1 ports of the sensors . A callout says See sheet 5/6.

Title block: Transit Priority Unit Cabinet Detail, sheet 1 of 6, City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation, Drawing No. S-70.3A. Drawn AN 12-01-01, checked AN 12-01-01, T. E. SS 01-01-01, Sr. T. E. SS 01-01-01, Pr. T. E. GO 2-14-01. Approved 2/20/2001, Frances T. Banerjee, General Manager. Printed page number 117.
notes:
1. This drawing depicts a two sensor configuration. Each sensor can accomodate up to two loops.

3. Route serial communications cable behind cabinet chasis. Connect 2070 cable end to the 2070 C21S port. Secure cable to cabinet chasis with wire ties.
Callouts: 2070 controller, Input File I, Input File J, 283LA sensor (see note 2), DB9 serial cable (see note 3), see sheet 5/6.
title: Transit Priority Unit Cabinet Detail - Front View
summary: Front view of the 2070 controller cabinet with the two 283LA transit sensors, drawing S-70.3A, sheet 1 of 6, approved 2/20/2001. It shows the 2070 controller above input files I and J, with the DB9 serial cable routed from the controller to the sensors. Three notes cover the two sensor configuration, sensor slots and serial cable routing.

description:

At the top is the 2070 controller with its rear connectors C2S, C21S, C12S, C11S, C20S, C22S, C1S and a DATA KEY. Below it are the input file backplane terminal blocks. The C20 harness (transit) and C2 harness (ATSAC) are labeled. A DB9 serial cable (see sheet 5/6) runs from the controller down to the C20 panel. The C20 panel (see sheet 6/6, see note 1) sits on the rack with TB0 (see sheets 4/6) just below it, and the C2 panel is below that. At the bottom, cabling labeled DLC to loops leaves the cabinet, which sits on a concrete base over ground shown with hatching.

title: Transit Priority Unit Cabinet Detail - Rear View
summary: Rear view of the 2070 controller cabinet showing the C20 transit harness and panel above the C2 panel, drawing S-70.3A, sheet 2 of 6. The section also shows the cabinet on a concrete base with the detector lead-in cable (DLC) running to the loops. One note says to install the C20 harness and panel on the rack above the C2 panel.

description:
Section detail, controller cabinet rear view (not to scale): Rear elevation of the cabinet. The 2070 controller rear panel shows connectors C2S, C21S, C12S, C11S, C20S, C22S, C1S and the data key. A DB9 serial cable (see note 1) runs from C21S down the left side. The C20 harness (see note 3, transit) comes from C20S and the C2 harness (ATSAC) is labeled below it. A power cable comes from the right side of the controller. On the terminal blocks, lugs at positions D, E, J and K are connected on both input file rows. The two input file harnesses (see note 2) run to a terminal panel at lower right with TB0 (see sheet 4/6).

Title block: Transit Priority Unit Cabinet Detail, sheet 3 of 6, City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation, Drawing No. S-70.3A. Printed page number 119.
notes:

title: Transit Priority Unit Cabinet Detail - Rear View with Harness Connections
summary: Rear view of the 2070 controller cabinet with the harness connections, drawing S-70.3A, sheet 3 of 6. It shows the DB9 serial cable on C21S, the C20 transit harness on C20S, the input file harness from TB0 to the input file backplane, and the power cable. Three notes cover those connections.

description:
12-position dual barrier strip TB0: A horizontal strip with 12 terminal positions, each with a top and bottom lug. Positions 1 to 3 are labeled NOT USED. Position 4 is GROUND and receives the DRAIN WIRES from the four cables. Positions 5 and 6 go TO PIN D and TO PIN E on the B1 harness (File I slot 10 backplane). Positions 7 and 8 go TO PIN J and TO PIN K on the B2 harness (File I slot 10 backplane). Positions 9 and 10 go TO PIN D and TO PIN E on the B3 harness (File J slot 10 backplane)*. Positions 11 and 12 go TO PIN J and TO PIN K on the B4 harness (File J slot 10 backplane)*.

Below the strip each pair of terminals is connected by a twisted pair to a cable end labeled B1, B2, B3* and B4*. These are the loop detector lead-in cables, labeled DLC (1-pair #12 AWG).

Footnote: * Second harness to input file J is only required for 3 and 4 loop installation.

Title block: Transit Priority Unit Cabinet Detail, sheet 4 of 6, City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation, Drawing No. S-70.3A. Printed page number 120.
notes:
1. All connections shall be soldered.
* Second harness to input file J is only required for 3 and 4 loop installation.
Callouts: B1 harness, B2 harness (file I slot 10 backplane); B3 harness, B4 harness (file J slot 10 backplane)*; GROUND; TO PIN D, E, J, K; NOT USED; DRAIN WIRES; DLC (1-pair #12 AWG); TB0.
title: Transit Priority Unit Cabinet Detail (12-Position Dual Barrier Strip Wiring)
summary: Wiring of the 12-position dual barrier strip TB0 in the transit priority unit cabinet, drawing S-70.3A, sheet 4 of 6. It shows which terminals take the ground and drain wires, which go to pins D, E, J and K of the input file slot 10 backplanes, and the detector lead-in cable (DLC) of 1 pair #12 AWG. One note says all connections shall be soldered.

The cable splits into two legs each with LENGTH = 1 FT., ending in DB9 male connectors labeled B1/B2 and B3/B4. These two connectors go to the 283LA sensor J1 port.

Pin table (PIN, FUNCTION 2070, FUNCTION 283 LA): 1, N/C, N/C. 2, TX, RX. 3, RX, TX. 4, N/C, N/C. 5, GND, GND. 6, N/C, N/C. 7, CTS, RTS. 8, RTS, CTS. 9, GND, GND.

Title block: Transit Priority Unit Cabinet Detail, sheet 5 of 6, City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation, Drawing No. S-70.3A. Printed page number 121.

Terminal panel: A 0.125 (1/8") white aluminum panel, 5.0" wide by 7.0" high with 1/2" radius corners. Two 1/4" mounting holes are at the top and bottom center (see note 1). CTB-4 is a 6-position dual barrier strip with positions N/C, N/C, AUDIO IN +, AUDIO IN -, AUDIO OUT + and AUDIO OUT -. The four audio terminals are labeled TO CTB-1. CTB-5 is an 8-position single barrier strip with positions +5V, -5V, CD, RTS, TX, RX, CTS and GND. Twisted wire pairs connect CTB-4 to the harness cable that leaves the panel at the lower right, and CTB-5 positions fan into the same cable.

C20 connector table (PIN, FUNCTION): A, AUDIO IN+. B, AUDIO IN-. C, AUDIO OUT+. D, +5 VDC. E, AUDIO OUT-. F, N/C. H, CD. J, RTS. K, TX. L, RX. M, CTS. N, DC GND. P, N/C. N, N/C (as drawn).

C20 harness: Isometric view of the connector body at left, with a harness (length = 6 FT) going to the 2070 controller (C20S port).

Title block: Transit Priority Unit Cabinet Detail, sheet 6 of 6, City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation, Drawing No. S-70.3A. Printed page number 122.
notes:
1. Provide two (2) 1/4" mounting holes centered 0.325" from top and bottom edges.
2. All connections shall be soldered.

description:
Upper plan view, channelized right turn at a right angle approach (no separate heading is printed above it): A triangular island between the right turn slip lane and the through lanes with integral curb and gutter, R=2' typical at the island tip. The island has 4' minimum on both sides of the ramp landing, a 5' minimum width, 2' minimum and 5' minimum dimensions at the crosswalk, and a 48" landing typical at the top of all curb ramps, see note 2. Landings are 2% max slope. Crosswalk cross slope along the turn is 2% typical, 5% max. The island edge along the slip lane is 20' minimum. The island approach angle is 55 degrees to 70 degrees. The turn lane is 11' minimum, 14' maximum (see note 1). Turn lane radius is R=150' to 275'. Corner radius is R=25' to 40', see corner radius policy. Bollard callout: if >9' wide, install bollard(s) in DWS at 2' maximum from the flow line, allowing a minimum of 4' path in between bollards (shown at two ramps). A unidirectional curb ramp without flares, typical, see S-442, serves the island and a parallel curb ramp, see S-442, serves the corner.

Lower plan view, constrained geometric design for channelized right turns: The same island layout with a tighter plan. It shows the 2' minimum, a 48" landing typical at top of all curb ramps (see note 2), a curb ramp typical (see S-442), 20' minimum island length, the 55 degree to 70 degree angle, an 11' minimum to 14' maximum turn lane (see note 1), 2% typical and 5% max crosswalk slope, R=2' typical, integral curb and gutter, turn lane R=150' to 275', narrow sidewalk (<=9'), and a parallel curb ramp, see S-442. Pavement markings are drawn in gray: crosswalk bars, a right turn arrow and a left turn arrow.

description:
Plan view, unconstrained geometric design for channelized right turns: A right turn slip lane with a raised island, bike lane, grass buffer and sidewalk along the curve. Across the top a bike lane crossing and a pedestrian crossing run side by side with a 3' minimum gap between them. A detectable warning surface is at the ramp, with 6' minimum and 4' minimum on both sides dimensions at the crossing, and a section cut A/2 through the island. A non-walkable surface, raised divisional island or curbing (typical) wraps the island with 5' minimum and 8' minimum dimensions at the crossing and R=5' minimum and R=10' minimum on the island corners. R=2' typical at the island tip, integral curb and gutter, and an 11' minimum to 14' maximum lane (see note 1). Other callouts: unidirectional curb ramp without flares, typical, see S-442. 55 degrees to 70 degrees island angle, 20' minimum, 4' minimum at the ramp. R=25' to 40', see corner radius policy. 150' to 275' radius at the outside of the turn. Labels along the curve: grass buffer, bike lane and sidewalk. (Optional) raised crosswalk and bike crossing, see Supplemental Design Guide Detail 600.

Section A (A/2), typical section at pedestrian/bicyclist island, steep road cross slopes, from left to right: repair or reconstruct street paving as necessary, 2' min, typical, then integral curb and gutter typical, a 6' MIN. non-walkable surface, a battered curb without gutter (TYP), see Supplemental Design Guide Detail 400, an 8' MIN. bike lane, a 3' space with non-walkable surface and a warning curb, a sidewalk curb ramp, a variable width island and the right turn lane, ending at an integral curb and gutter.

description:
Plan, mountable truck apron, directional curb ramps located outside truck apron: A corner with the street flowline and an outer face of curb with radius R2 (15' typical) and an inner curb with radius R1. The gray apron between the two curves is the mountable truck apron, 5' MIN. and 15' MAX. wide. Points of curvature and tangency are labeled for R1 and R2. Mountable curb, see note 1, runs along the outer edge. The inner edge is a curb with 3" min. curb height, see note 2. The mountable truck apron is also tied to note 4. Directional curb ramps are placed outside the apron on each leg. The ramp note reads curb ramp, typ, directional curb ramp shown, but may vary based on available sidewalk space, see S-442. Integral curb and gutter, see S-410. A crosswalk is shown as gray bars. Section cut A/1 is marked at the outer curb.

Section A/1, apron section, 1 tier apron: From left to right, repair or reconstruct street paving as necessary, 2' min, then the flow line, see note 3, then the mountable curb, see sheet 2. The mountable truck apron width varies (5' min, 15' max) and slopes 0.25% MIN to 1% MAX, see note 6, toward the flow line. The apron is 8" concrete, see note 4, on 8" min subbase. A curb, see note 2, stands 3" MIN. above the apron, see note 2, and separates it from the sidewalk.

description:
Plan view of the transition: A horizontal street centerline is drawn as a dash-dot line. The transition starts at point A at the left (START OF TRANSITION) where the striping leaves the centerline on a 30:1 taper. The tapered line runs 27 m (90') to point B and the overall length to the end of transition is 45 m (150'). A smooth S curve then moves the line across the centerline to point H at the end of transition. Points B and C, E and F, I and J are used to form two curves, B-J-E and F-I-H. Along the baseline from B to the end of transition the segments are 3 m (10'), 3 m (10'), 6 m (20'), 3 m (10') and 3 m (10'). At the end of transition the lateral offsets are 1.5 m (5') from point D to the centerline and 3 m (10') between points D and H. Thick segments mark the striping lines at start and end. Dashed construction lines connect A to D and C to G, and points D, G and H are the layout points.

Procedure to install transition: see the numbered steps in the notes.

Title block: City of Pasadena, Public Works & Transportation Department, Turn Bay Transition, Single Double Centerline. Drawn by M. Mojica, checked by D. Ortega, submitted by C. Hernandez. Approved by the Transportation Administrator, RTE No. 1820, expires June 30, 2005, dated 6/4/01. Revision 1, Units DUAL, Standard Plan S-702, sheet 1 of 1.
notes:
Procedure to install transition:
1. Layout points A, D, G, & H.
2. Use points A & D to determine a straight line and mark B & C.
3. Use points C & G to determine a straight line and mark E & F.
4. Mark J by measuring 180 mm (7") in from C. Mark I by measuring 150 mm (6") in from G.
5. Form curves B-J-E & F-I-H.
6. Stripe.
title: Turn Bay Transition - Single or Double Centerline
summary: City of Pasadena standard plan S-702, revision 1, dual units, dated 6/4/01. It lays out a left turn bay transition from the centerline of the street with a 30:1 taper from point A over a 45 m (150 ft) length, and gives a six step procedure to mark points A through J and form the curves.
